The result is a request dispatch primitive that turns intended GET calls into arbitrary methods such as POST, PUT, or DELETE. Technical details The root cause is classified under CWE-1321 (Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes) and CWE-454 (External Initialization of Trusted Variables or Data Stores). In lib/core/Axios.js, the method fallback chain reads this.defaults.method without an own-property guard: config.method = (config.method || this.defaults.method || 'get').toLowerCase();. If Object.prototype.method has been polluted by a separate vulnerability in the same Node.js process, the fallback resolves to the attacker-controlled value. The same inherited-property pattern also affects this.defaults.allowAbsoluteUrls, which can alter how absolute URLs are combined with baseURL. Exploitation requires a pre-existing prototype pollution primitive elsewhere in the application — Axios itself is the read-side gadget, not the pollution source (GitHub Advisory). Impact Successful chained exploitation allows an attacker to force Axios default-instance requests that omit an explicit method (e.g., axios.request({ url }) or axios({ url })) to send state-changing HTTP verbs such as DELETE, POST, PUT, or PATCH instead of the safe default GET.
